title: The Siege of 1453, Step by Step
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Step through eight turning points of the 1453 siege of Constantinople on a schematic map and attribute each to the defense it defeated, or recognize that the defenders held.

educational.topic: The Siege of 1453, Step by Step
learningObjectives: Attribute each of eight turning points of the 1453 siege to the defense of Constantinople it overcame, or recognize that the defenders held, with at least 6 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The Bosphorus Strait and the Golden Horn
The Theodosian Walls, moat and breach
The chain across the Golden Horn
Mehmed II, Constantine XI and Giovanni Giustiniani Longo

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through with prediction before each reveal (attribution)
keyQuestions: Which of the city's defenses does this event defeat?
Which defenses were already gone before the final assault?
On which days did the defenders win?
commonMisconceptions: The city fell only because of the cannon.
The ships dragged overland broke into the city from the harbor.
Everything in the siege went Mehmed's way.
The West sent help that was defeated.
The defenders were a large army.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on eight steps (mastery: 6 of 8).
Explain why the ships hauled overland mattered although they never attacked the sea walls.
